_comment: One entry = one behaviour of one hook-level check, broken in isolation.
`find` must match EXACTLY ONCE in `file`; a drifted pattern is reported, not skipped silently.
`replace` must leave the file valid Go — deleting a block often orphans a variable, so prefer
neutering a condition (`&& false`, `|| true`, `_ = x`) over removing lines.
`known_gap` marks a mutation nothing catches ON PURPOSE: an equivalent mutant, or a real hole
recorded rather than implied away. Without it, --strict fails on the survivor.

mutations.known_gap: Equivalent mutant in isolation, and deliberately so: fired.Violations is assigned from len(violations)>0, so on unmutated bookkeeping the two spellings agree. It is defense in depth against a SECOND mutation, and only observable compounded with one. Compound it with qualified/provenance and go-samerepo-missing-selector-asks fails with 'expected an ask, got a defer' -- the ask is dropped outright rather than mislabelled, which is what gating on the merged slice makes impossible. Kept as a survivor with this note rather than deleted, because a future edit that reverts the gate would otherwise leave no trace of why it was written this way.
